'''Arnold Lockshin''' (born February 3, 1939) is an American-born Russian scientist. After he was dismissed from a position as a cancer researcher in [[Houston, Texas]], he and his family received [[political asylum]] and citizenship in the [[Soviet Union]]. The film director [[Michael Lockshin (film director)|Michael Lockshin]] is his son.

==Early life==
Lockshin was born in San Francisco.<ref name=FLS/> His ancestors on his father's side were Soviet Jews who fled to escape antisemitic persecution.<ref>{{cite web |last=Recer |first=Paul |date=October 9, 1986 |title=Defector Underwent Troubling, Unexplained Change, Boss Says |url=https://apnews.com/article/340efaa24201571ec560266341815f5f |website=[[AP NEWS]] |access-date=6 May 2023 |language=en}}</ref> He attended high school in [[Richmond, California]], and graduated in 1956. He attended the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and earned an undergraduate degree in biochemistry.<ref name=TPP>{{cite news|title=Defector at peace in Moscow|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1144&dat=19870505&id=wMobAAAAIBAJ&pg=6752,3130734|access-date=October 5, 2014|work=[[The Pittsburgh Press]]|date=May 5, 1987}}</ref> He completed a doctorate in biochemistry at the [[University of Wisconsin]].<ref name=Montgomery>{{cite news|last1=Montgomery|first1=Dave|title=Defectors find they miss country music|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1987/04/21/defectors-find-they-miss-country-music/|access-date=October 5, 2014|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=April 21, 1987}}</ref>

==Early career==
Lockshin performed cancer research at the [[Keck School of Medicine of USC|USC School of Medicine]] between 1977 and 1980. From 1980 to 1986, Lockshin worked at the Stehlin Foundation, a cancer research facility associated with [[St. Joseph Medical Center (Houston, Texas)|St. Joseph Hospital]] in Houston. He was terminated from that position.<ref name=FLS>{{cite news|last1=Smale|first1=Alison|title=Researcher claims harassment prompted defection|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1298&dat=19861009&id=A4QwAAAAIBAJ&pg=7322,1564685|access-date=October 5, 2014|work=[[The Free Lance–Star]]|date=October 9, 1986}}</ref>

Leadership at the Stehlin Foundation said that he was fired because of his deteriorating work performance. Lockshin said that the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] was involved in his firing and that he and his family had been the targets of death threats and other forms of harassment.<ref name=TPP/> Lockshin said that he and his wife had long supported [[socialism]] and that he had previously been a [[Communist Party USA]] organizer.  [[Dorothy Ray Healey|Dorothy Healey]] described his Party role as a district organizer, calling him "a rigid dogmatist".<ref name=Healey>{{cite book|last1=Healey|first1=Dorothy|title=California Red: A life in the American Communist Party|date=1993|publisher=University of Illinois Press|isbn=9780252062780|page=237|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vO5lJouCyPUC&q=Arnold+lockshin&pg=PA237|access-date=5 October 2014}}</ref> He said that the government harassment was brought on by his political beliefs.<ref name=Hendersonville>{{cite news|last1=Smale|first1=Alison|title=Lockshin says he was Communist organizer|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1665&dat=19861011&id=MzAaAAAAIBAJ&pg=5407,2345780|access-date=October 5, 2014|work=[[Times-News (Hendersonville, North Carolina)|Times-News]]|date=October 11, 1986}}</ref><ref name=TM>{{cite news|last1=Jarboe|first1=Jan|title=Red Square|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pSsEAAAAMBAJ&q=Arnold+lockshin&pg=PA50 |access-date=October 5, 2014|work=[[Texas Monthly]]|date=July 1982}}</ref>

==Political asylum==
The USSR leadership provided them with the requested asylum, gave Lockshin an apartment in Moscow and assisted him in securing employment.{{Citation needed|date=May 2011}} Subsequently, he and his wife Lauren gave numerous interviews and press-conferences in Moscow accusing American [[secret services]] of persecuting [[dissidents]] in the [[United States]].<ref>''Pravda'' Oct 11, 1986, p.2  as translated in ''Current Digest of the Soviet Press'' [https://books.google.com/books?id=uN8oAQAAMAAJ&q=Arnold+lockshin Google Books excerpt]</ref> In 1989 they published a book, in Russian, as well as English, titled ''Silent Terror: One family's history of political persecution in the United States''.<ref>{{cite book | title=Silent Terror: One family's history of political persecution in the United States | first1=Arnold | last1=Lockshin | first2=Lauren | last2=Lockshin | publisher=[[RIA Novosti|АПН]] | year=1988 | pages=173 | isbn=5-7020-0042-0 }}</ref><ref>(Russian title: ''Безмолвный террор: история политического преследования семьи в Соединенных Штатах'') ''(Bezmolvnyĭ terror : istorii︠a︡ politicheskogo presledovanii︠a︡ semʹi v Soedinennykh Shtatakh)'' Moskva : Izd-vo Agenstva pechati Novosti, 1989. [https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/29979441 WorldCat item record]</ref>

==Later life==
In 1992 Lockshin received Russian citizenship by order of Russian president [[Boris Yeltsin]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Berliner |first=Jeff |date=9 August 1992 |title=American defector wins Russian citizenship |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1992/08/09/American-defector-wins-Russian-citizenship/5451713332800/ |access-date=2025-07-24 |work=[[United Press International|UPI]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=6 August 1992 |title=Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 06.08.1992 г. № 835 О приеме в гражданство Российской Федерации Локшина А. |trans-title=Decree of the President of the Russian Federation No. 835 on Granting Citizenship to Lokshin A. |url=http://kremlin.ru/acts/bank/1757 |access-date= |publisher=Kremlin.ru |language=ru}}</ref> Lockshin continued to work in the Blokhin Oncological Scientific Center in Moscow as a research biologist until the late 1990s.

Subsequently, Arnold and Lauren disappeared from public view. Their current whereabouts are unknown. However, at least two of their children appear currently to live in Russia, including his daughter, Jennifer, who works at the [[State University – Higher School of Economics]]. Their son, [[Michael Lockshin (film director)|Michael]], is a Russian film director known for his film ''[[The Master and Margarita (2024 film)|The Master and Margarita]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dolin |first1=Anton |title="Серебряные коньки» — российский сказочный ромком с либеральными идеями от сценариста «Эпидемии" |url=https://meduza.io/feature/2020/12/10/serebryanye-konki-rossiyskiy-skazochnyy-romkom-s-liberalnymi-ideyami-ot-stsenarista-epidemii |website=Meduza |access-date=27 May 2022}}</ref><ref name="komsomolets" /> In an interview in 2017, Arnold Lockshin said that he had separated from his wife at some point after moving.<ref name="komsomolets">{{cite web |title=Сбежавшая из США в СССР семья Локшиных пережила крутые метаморфозы |url=https://www.mk.ru/social/2017/04/17/sbezhavshaya-iz-ssha-v-sssr-semya-lokshinykh-perezhila-krutye-metamorfozy.html |website=Moskovskij Komsomolets |date=April 17, 2017 |access-date=26 May 2022}}</ref>

On July 21, 2013, Arnold Lockshin appeared on a TV talk-show hosted by [[Igor Vittel]] on the Russian RBC channel and spoke in support of political asylum for [[Edward Snowden]].{{citation needed|date=May 2014}}
